correctness.rationale: The uniform-seed outbreak mean is 1+(2/n)Σ_{unordered u,v}p^{distance}, because tree percolation connects exactly along the unique path. Deleting edge e removes cross-cut pairs and maximizes F_e(p)=product of endpoint-distance generating functions. A separate independent networkx unlabelled-tree enumeration (counts 1,1,2,3,6,11,23 for n2..8) computed every cut polynomial by explicit vertex-pair distances. It found uniform integer Bernstein-basis certificates for every class through7 and 21 of 23 eight-vertex classes, and exactly two exception classes. For Type I alternative-center difference p(1-p-p^2); Type II p(1-2p), with all other edges dominated, establishing exact transitions golden ratio conjugate and 1/2. Nonnegative Bernstein integer coefficients guarantee all real p in [0,1], not sample points.

These are credited, not new here. On the user-specified different functional (mean uniformly seeded finite-tree cluster under one preemptive edge removal), the complete first order and only two exceptional topologies require a new classification. Enns link-removal intervention models use other optimization assumptions.
